overview.headline: Drag depends on air density velocity shape and reference area

keyPoints.point: Drag grows with air density and with the square of velocity
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity

keyPoints.point: Variable can collect complex effects into an equation for drag
keyPoints.quote: This allows us to collect all the effects, simple and complex, into a single equation.

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficient includes form drag skin friction wave drag and induced drag
keyPoints.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficients are determined experimentally using a wind tunnel for given shapes
keyPoints.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyTerms.gloss: variable that collects effects for drag into an equation
keyTerms.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyTerms.gloss: area used to characterize dependence on body size
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: combined terms called pressure in Bernoulli pressure equation
keyTerms.quote: is called the dynamic pressure and appears in Bernoulli’s pressure equation.

keyTerms.gloss: property named density shown by rho not by letter for distance
keyTerms.quote: We do not use “d” for density since “d” is often used to specify distance.
